VERDANT INTEROPERABILITY TEST PLAN V1.0

Objective

The plan verifies that connectors at SolCentro, NEXUS, and Instituto Técnico do Norte exchange catalogues and products according to schemas, policies, and controls. Initial runs use synthetic data. Real products are enabled after privacy and security close.

Environments

Development supports local tests; integration connects services with synthetic data; pilot uses authorized networks and certificates. Configurations have a version and checksum. Every test states its environment.

Criteria

Every case contains preconditions, identity, product, operation, input, expected result, audit record, cleanup, and owner. Failures are blocking, major, or minor. An authorization error, exposure, or acceptance of a revoked certificate is blocking.

Sequence

It begins with health, catalogue, and authentication; continues with authorization, products, errors, and withdrawal; and ends with performance, rollback, and deletion.

Test case 1

Case 1: Health. The expected result is that all services and dependencies respond. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored. Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible.

Test case 2

Case 2: Catalogue. The expected result is that the consumer discovers only visible products. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored. Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible.

Test case 3

Test case 13

The coverage matrix links every requirement to a case. Critical controls have both an allowed and denied test. A requirement without a test remains open.

Test case 14

The report records date, environment, versions, person, results, and evidence. Screenshots contain no secrets. Values used in integration are synthetic.

Test case 15

Pilot entry requires zero blocking failures, closure of network, logging, rotation, and revocation controls, and approval of aggregation. Minor failures may be accepted with an owner and date.
